answer: An identity registers only by posting a bond of 50 units against one attested hardware credential, and each registration writes a hash to a delta log. Forging N identities locks 50N units for 20 epochs, with 100% slashed on proven duplication. Splitting one credential into many keys raises marginal bond cost per fake identity and triggers slashing across the shared attestation, flagged by independent jurors who cross-check the marble ledger and an echo record.
